significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) predictive coupling that a residual-stream quantity at the “</think> boundary” predicts prompt harmfulness better than visible chain-of-thought and forecasts later verdict/output dissociation, together with the form-(ii) claim that “re-assert[ing] the latent verdict at the answer boundary suppresses silent overrides.” This would establish both a behavioral phenomenon and a candidate mechanism, materially constraining when safety-relevant information becomes available and whether answer generation can reverse it; that matters given Turpin et al. (2023) on unfaithful CoT and Arditi et al. (2024) on causally actionable refusal directions. However, the claim trains the verdict to predict request harmfulness, so “harmful latent verdict paired with a refusing output” ordinarily denotes correct harm recognition rather than a “faked refusal”; the core predictive hypothesis has distinguishable true/false states, but the stronger interpretation of these mismatches as internal safety intentions is underdetermined, and a negative result would rule out this particular boundary-verdict account rather than latent monitoring generally. Topic-substitution check: generic mechanistic LLM safety would not earn this score; the above-median value comes specifically from the asserted boundary-time predictive coupling and answer-phase reversal mechanism.

reach.justification: The named handles are a “latent thinking-block monitor” and a “minimal intervention that re-asserts the latent verdict at the answer boundary”; the former is ex ante because it is “available before the answer is generated,” leaving time to gate or modify generation, while the latter is an actionable decode-time control. The conclusion asserts a transferable relation—boundary projection outperforming CoT monitoring and predicting answer-phase failures—so after per-model re-extraction it predicts what researchers should find rather than merely supplying a search procedure. Its stated scope covers reasoning models and multiple attack families, and the downstream users include model auditors and deployment teams, although applicability is restricted by the acknowledged focus on open models with explicit thinking tags and the semantic ambiguity of the verdict limits use as an intent detector. Topic-substitution check: removing the boundary monitor, lead time, and re-assertion handle leaves only generic LLM-safety aspirations, which would not support this reach score.
